To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a simple and fast gas chromatographic method with mass spectrometric detection was validated to determine fenamidone residue in grapes and wines, and that the EURACHEM global uncertainty budget gave lower estimates than the ones obtained from the Horowitz function.

we validated a simple and fast gas chromatographic with tandem mass spectrometry (GC-MS/MS) method for analysis of fenamidones in grapes and wines and we also assessed the global uncertainty of the GC-MS/MS method.

the proposed gas chromatographic with tandem mass spectrometry (GC-MS) method is suitable to quantify fenamidone at low concentrations in grapes and wines and its global uncertainty was estimated and found to be below 25%.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a simple and fast method for fenamadone analysis in grapes, and wines that is also suitable for routine use.
the determination of fenamidones in grapes and wines by gas chromatography-mass spectrometry.
the validation and global uncertainty estimation for a method to determine fenamidone.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

fenamidone can be determined in grapes and wines by gas chromatography coupled with mass spectrometric detection with a global uncertainty below 25% and with a limit of detection of 0.05-0.06 mg/kg or mg/L, respectively.
this method is suitable for the determination of fenamidones in grapes and wines at the levels expected in routine analysis.
the global uncertainty of the method was below 25%, with an uncertainty of the mean value below 10% for concentrations between 0.05 and 1.00mg/kg (or mg/l) of fenamadone.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
this gas chromatographic with a mass spectrometry technique is a simple, fast and accurate method to analyze fenamide in grapes and wine.
this method fulfills the requirements of the European Commission Regulation (EU) No 543/2011, and the uncertainty of the method is acceptable.
the global uncertainty of the method was acceptable, and that this uncertainty could be reduced by increasing the number of samples analyzed.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, in addition to being a simple, fast and reliable method, this work provides a useful tool to assess global uncertainty of a method for a specific pesticide, which is a key element in the development of a harmonized pesticide residue analysis.
the EURACHEM global uncertainty budget is more suitable to calculate the uncertainty in pesticide residue analysis.
the method proposed is suitable for the analysis of fenamidones in grapes and wines, and that the global uncertainty is low enough for its use in residue monitoring programs.
